question: Which kills the most people each year: sharks, dogs, mosquitoes or snakes? Put them in order.
answer: Mosquitoes, by far. Malaria alone killed about 597,000 people in 2023, most of them small children in Africa. Snakebites kill at least 81,000 people a year and dogs about 59,000, almost all through rabies. Sharks kill around six. The animal with the films is not the one doing the killing.
move: Fear follows the scary story; the danger follows the numbers.

items.label: Sharks
items.note: About six a year. Malaria kills that many roughly every five minutes.

items.label: Dogs
items.note: Almost all through rabies, which a vaccine after the bite prevents.

items.label: Mosquitoes
items.note: Malaria alone, in 2023. Most of the dead were children under five.

items.label: Snakes
items.note: At least 81,000, and maybe 138,000: most bites are far from any antivenom.

source: WHO, World Malaria Report 2024 and fact sheets on snakebite and rabies; Florida Museum, International Shark Attack File

question: Which takes the most water to make one kilogram: beef, chocolate, cheese, rice or tomatoes?
answer: Chocolate, just ahead of beef. A kilogram of chocolate takes about 17,000 litres, most of it rain on cocoa farms, against 15,400 for beef, 5,060 for cheese, 2,500 for rice and 214 for tomatoes. Most of each figure is rain that would have fallen anyway; the water pumped from rivers is a much smaller share.
move: A food's water bill is mostly the rain on the fields that grew it.

items.label: Rice
items.note: Paddy fields are flooded, yet rice needs a seventh of what chocolate does.

items.label: Beef
items.note: Mostly the rain on the fields that grow three years of the animal's feed.

items.label: Tomatoes
items.note: A tomato plant gives a lot of fruit, and the fruit is mostly water.

items.label: Cheese
items.note: It takes about ten litres of milk to make one kilogram of cheese.

items.label: Chocolate
items.note: Cocoa trees yield little: a kilogram of chocolate needs a lot of beans.

source: Mekonnen & Hoekstra, Water Footprint Network product gallery
reference: Mekonnen, M.M. & Hoekstra, A.Y. (2012) A global assessment of the water footprint of farm animal products, Ecosystems 15: 401–415; https://www.waterfootprint.org/resources/interactive-tools/product-gallery/

question: Per kilogram, which puts the most greenhouse gas into the air: beef, dark chocolate, coffee, cheese or chicken?
answer: Beef, by a long way: about 100 kg of greenhouse gas for every kilogram. Then come dark chocolate at 47 kg and coffee at 29 kg, mostly from forest cleared to plant them, ahead of cheese at 24 kg and chicken at 10. A kilogram of chocolate lasts a lot longer than a kilogram of steak, though.
move: Compare foods by the kilogram you actually eat, not by the label.

items.label: Chicken
items.note: A tenth of beef: chickens turn feed into meat far more efficiently.

items.label: Cheese
items.note: Ten litres of milk go into a kilogram, and dairy cows belch methane too.

items.label: Beef
items.note: Cattle belch methane, and their pasture is often cleared forest.

items.label: Coffee
items.note: Most of it is land use: forest cleared for coffee farms.

items.label: Dark chocolate
items.note: Nearly half of beef, mostly from rainforest cleared for cocoa.

source: Poore & Nemecek, Science (2018), via Our World in Data
reference: Poore, J. & Nemecek, T. (2018) Reducing food's environmental impacts through producers and consumers, Science 360: 987–992; https://ourworldindata.org/environmental-impacts-of-food
